If you're injured in a car accident that was a result of someone else's fault or negligence, you might deserve compensation for any lost wages, medical expenses or emotional damage you may have undergone. However, such cases aren't always as straightforward. The insurance company and other vested interests will very likely always be on the lookout for reasons to justify offering you a much lower settlement sum. Therefore, you should ensure that any actions you take in dealing with the insurance company, or in fact any party to the accident, should be done in the presence or, or under the guidance of your personal injury attorney

Here are 5 common mistakes people make that can reduce the value of their personal injury claim.

  1. Not reporting the accident to the police immediately

Involving the authorities immediately after an accident will enable you to have an official police report that will likely help tilt the case in your favor. The police will usually take photographs of the scene and interview witnesses to the accident. The report they write will act as evidence, providing as much details regarding the accident, as well as any circumstance surrounding it.

A police record will also document essential details about the accident that you may not be able to recall. Sometimes your memory may fail you months or years down the line after an accident. And hopefully, if you are truly not at fault, then such police report will go a long way in proving your innocence in the accident, thereby making it much easier for your attorney to seek compensation for you.

  1. Failing to attend any of your medical appointments:

Of course, it goes without saying that you should seek medical attention right after the accident, even after a minor accident. How else will you prove the existence and extent of your injuries? Without a medical report from a qualified physician, there is very little chance of a case. But seeking treatment is not enough in itself. You should also follow every single recommendation your physician makes for your treatment and attend all your medical appointments. If you demonstrate a lack of concern in getting better, the court might care less about awarding you compensation.

  1. Posting on social media:

Even something as harmless as updating your status on Facebook can affect your personal injury case significantly. You should be very careful with what you post on your social media because the defense attorney will be happy and ready to use it against you in your case. If you're seeking compensation for any physical or emotional damage as a result of the accident, you can't afford to post images that may present you as being as happy and healthy as ever.

Positive posts and images may discredit any claims you make in court. If possible, you should consider temporarily suspending your use of social media during the case. If that seems hard to do, you should at least maintain the highest standards of privacy including not accepting any new friends until the litigation finally ends.

  1. Acting in the absence of your lawyer:

The insurance company may come to you early on in the process and ask you to sign different forms for this and that. Don't fall for their trickery. Although the documents may seem unassuming, they may be banking on the chance that you will never read or scrutinize them well enough. One simple signature can wave away your right to a fair or even any compensation and absolve the insurance company from any liability.

If you must sign anything, it must be in the presence of your car accident injury lawyer. In any case, any qualified attorney will tell you that accepting early compensations will almost always get you a raw deal. Even when you aren't signing documents, avoid discussing anything about the accident with the insurance company or its representatives. Most importantly, never give them a recorded statement. They can trick you into admitting things that will eventually hurt your case.

  1. Misrepresenting information:

Any information you submit to parties involved in your case, whether to your doctor, the court or your lawyer, should be 100% accurate and true. Any false information you give may come back to hurt your credibility, and sometimes it won't matter how solid the rest of your case is or how much evidence you have. Remember the insurance company will do their own private investigation. They will subpoena your medical records and conduct surveillance to gather every bit of information they can to weaken your case.

In summary

If you get involved in a car accident, call for medical attention immediately and make sure to inform the police or relevant authorities. Avoid talking to the insurance company or making any deals in the absence of your injury lawyer. Be careful with what you post on your social media and be honest with the court, your doctor and your lawyer. Most importantly, ensure that you hire a qualified car accident injury lawyer who will ensure you receive your deserved compensation.
